III. DESCRIPTION OF COMPLETED PROJECT
I. General
Upon the completion of all scheduled activities outlined in the project's urban renewal plan, certain physical and demographic changes will have occurred within the project area. These physical changes are designed to bring about an improvement in the social and economic climate of the project area, and thus create a positive influence over other surrounding areas as well.
2. Land Use and Population Density
A change in the land use for some portions of the project area will have the general effect of converting the area from commericial/professional to residential in character. The proposed land use plan (see Proposed Land Use Map, appendix C) also calls for decreasing the density of population in certain Sections of the present residential area east of Second Street. (Also see the "Disposition Map," appendix CC for the type of redevelopment sheeduled for each.) This change in land use will also accomplish another primary objective of the plan (see Part II); that of redevelopment of property consistent with accepted measures, e.g. clearance of areas, and subsequent redevelopment under a comprehensive flood plain ordinance, to lessen the effects of future flooding should the area once again be flooded. This action is termed "flood conservation."
Along Front Street, five major parcels, i.e., one or more properties at the specific location, will be acquired by the Redevelopment Authority, cleared and sold for redevelopment or retained by the City for public use (see Land Acquisition Map, appendix H). Four of these parcels will be sold for redevelopment as residential-general. To legally permit this proposed land use the present zoning for the area Will require revision (see Existing and Proposed Zoning Map appendix G).
Residential-general is a land use that will permit three to four story medium-rise apartments. Judging from the size of the parcels-There will be less than 100 dwelling units each.
The new construction that will result from the redevelopment of these parcels will be required to conform to proposed Flood Plain Ordinances. The proposed ordinances include, among other things, an amendment to the local building codes requiring all new structures in the designated flood plain or flood way area to be elevated or floodproofing in their design (see excerpts from proposed ordinance, appendix K). New flood plain and flood way areas are, being established by the Federal Insurance Administration (FIA). Adherence to this new set of building regulations may cause some deviation from the style of architecture now found in contemporary buildings in the area.
